viewsWelcome.contents:
The effective DB tables (game + mod list) appear here once the game is known. Start a Total War debug session, or set up the game first.
[Open DB Table…](command:twdev.openDbTable)

packfilesDirectory.description: Folder (relative to the workspace) that contains the files to pack into your mod.

modName.description: Name of the packfile, for example my_mod.pack.

executable.description: Path to the Total War executable, for example C:/Games/steamapps/common/Total War WARHAMMER III/Warhammer3.exe. The pack is installed into its data folder.

game.description: Game key used to build the pack. Defaults to the twdev.game setting.

addToUsedMods.description: Add the mod to the used mod list file.

modListFile.description: Name of the used mod list file.

includeDebuggerMod.description: Also install the debugger mod shipped with the extension and add it to the mod list file.

dependencies.description: Mods this mod needs. When set, the task writes the whole mod list file (modListFile): these mods, the debugger mod (includeDebuggerMod) and this mod, with this mod taking priority. Do not point modListFile at used_mods.txt.

anyOf.description: A Steam Workshop item id (e.g. "2789857593", must be subscribed), a pack in the game's data folder ("some_mod.pack") or a path to a pack file ("D:/mods/other_mod.pack").
A mod you develop: packed from a folder before every launch.

folder.description: Folder with the mod's files (like this project's packfilesDirectory), relative to the workspace.

twdev.game.description: Game used to read and build pack files.

twdev.addVirtualFolderOnDebug.description: In multi-root workspaces, add the "Virtual TW Source Files" folder (the Lua files inside the game's packs) when a debug session starts. In a single folder window use the "TotalWar: Show Virtual Source Files" command.

twdev.dbSchemaPath.markdownDescription: RPFM schema used to decode DB tables: a `schema_<game>.ron` file, or a folder with them (e.g. RPFM's `schemas` folder). Empty: download it from rpfm-schemas (refreshed daily), falling back to the copy shipped with the extension.

enumDescriptions: Only while a Total War debug session runs.
Whenever a Lua file is open.
twdev.dbHover.description: Hovering a string in Lua that is a DB key (unit, building, effect, ...) shows its effective row.

enumDescriptions: Never: a missing Workshop dependency stops the launch with a link to subscribe yourself.
twdev.autoSubscribeDependencies.markdownDescription: When a `pack` task's Workshop dependencies (or the items they require) are not downloaded, subscribe to them through Steam and wait for the download. Steam must be running.

enumDescriptions: The binary file the game reads, as RPFM writes it.
RPFM's TSV text format (`<name>.tsv`): readable diffs and merges in git. The pack task converts it to binary.
twdev.newTableFormat.markdownDescription: Format of DB tables and loc files made with **New DB Table…** and **New Loc File…**. Both open in the same editor.

twdev.modDiagnostics.markdownDescription: In mod projects, check the DB tables and loc files in the workspace and list problems in the Problems view: tables of an older version than the game's, references to keys that do not exist, repeated keys, new rows without loc text. **TotalWar: Check Mod DB Tables and Loc Files** checks now.

twdev.dbCompletion.description: In Lua strings, complete DB keys (units, buildings, effects, ...) and make known keys Ctrl+clickable to open their row. Indexes all DB tables of the game and mod list once, in the background.

twdev.virtualFiles.exclude.markdownDescription: Files of the game's and the mods' packs to leave out of **Virtual TW Source Files**: glob patterns relative to a pack, any case (`audio`, `*.wem`, `ui/skins/**`, `**/*.{anim,meta}`). A pattern without `/` matches a name in any folder; a folder hides everything in it. Folders left empty are not shown. Hidden files still open from the debugger and links. **TotalWar: Filter Virtual Files…** sets this by kind of file.

twdev.hotReload.markdownDescription: While the game is connected, run a mod script again in the game when you save it. Listeners it adds are added again: guard them (`core:remove_listener` first) or use this for scripts that only define functions.

twdev.eventMonitor.exclude.markdownDescription: Script events the **TotalWar: Start/Stop Event Monitor** leaves out of the `TW Script Events` output (names, `*` matches anything).

twdev.profiler.interval.markdownDescription: The profiler records the Lua call stack every this many Lua VM instructions. Smaller is more precise and slows the game more.
